name: SafeStep Apex Fauna Deterrent AFD-6 'Wardoff'
description:
The AFD-6 is SafeStep's purpose-built response to one of Meridian 88's more specific hazards: the proliferation of genetically modified and cybernetically augmented animals in urban environments. Geneware modification of domestic and feral animals has produced a generation of creatures that are larger, faster, more aggressive, and in some cases more intelligent than their baseline counterparts — and standard OC or capsaicin sprays that would deter a baseline dog are largely ineffective against a gene-uplifted rottweiler with pain-tolerance modifications or a feral cat pack with enhanced predator instincts. The AFD-6 addresses this gap through a dual-compound formula: a synthetic aversive olfactory compound targeting the heightened chemoreceptors common in gene-modified animals, combined with a secondary neurological disruption agent calibrated to the modified nervous system profiles documented in licensed geneware registries.

The canister is ruggedized for outdoor and sub-level use, with a waterproof housing, belt-clip retention system, and a single large actuator designed to be operated with gloves or augmented hands. The spray produces a visible orange-tinted mist with a sharp acrid odor that humans find unpleasant but tolerable — for a gene-modified animal with chemoreception augmentation, the olfactory component alone is described in SafeStep's testing data as producing immediate flight response in 94% of documented subjects. The neurological component handles the remaining cases, including cybered animals whose olfactory systems have been partially replaced with electronic sensors.

The AFD-6 is widely used in Meridian's sub-level infrastructure zones, where feral gene-mod animal populations have established territories in abandoned transit tunnels and drainage systems. Utility workers, Shelf residents, and infrastructure maintenance crews consider it standard kit.
legality: Legal — unrestricted civilian sale; classified as animal deterrent, not weapon
specifications:
Active compounds: SS-Avers-6 (olfactory aversive) + SS-NeuroD-6 (neurological disruptor, gene-mod calibrated)
Effective range: 3m stream
Onset: 1–2 seconds (olfactory); 3–5 seconds (neurological)
Duration of effect: 10–20 minutes
Canister capacity: 10 bursts
Weight: 0.21 kg
Dimensions: 15cm × 4.5cm
Housing: IP67 waterproof, impact-resistant polymer
Price: Φ48
tactical_use: Utility workers and infrastructure teams clip AFD-6 to harnesses before descending into sub-level zones. In encounters with gene-mod feral animals, the standard practice is a single burst aimed at the animal's face or approach path — the olfactory compound creates an immediate aversion barrier that most animals will not cross. For cybered animals with reduced olfactory sensitivity, a sustained burst allows the neurological component to take effect. Shelf residents in animal-territory blocks keep them mounted near doorframes. Some courier services operating in contested sub-level routes mandate AFD-6 as minimum personal equipment.
cultural_context: Wardoff is the kind of product that earns loyalty through necessity rather than enthusiasm. In Shelf communities adjacent to gene-mod feral territory, it is kept next to the door the same way older generations kept umbrellas — a mundane precaution against a mundane hazard that can nonetheless ruin your day. Sub-level workers have a saying: 'You don't need to be faster than the dog, you just need your Wardoff.' The orange mist has become an informal territorial marker in some sub-level zones — the smell of a recent AFD-6 deployment tells experienced travelers that something dangerous passed through recently.
known_users: Shelf residents in feral-territory adjacent zones
story_hooks: Someone has been systematically buying out AFD-6 stock across three Shelf districts — and the gene-mod feral population in those sectors has been growing unusually aggressive
